4786-zone-policeman-88-a-close-range-stu.title: A Close Range Study Of The Panama Canal And Its Workers
4786-zone-policeman-88-a-close-range-stu.creator: Unknown
4786-zone-policeman-88-a-close-range-stu.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. road flat desk, then out the wide-open window and across the shimmering roofs of Ancon to the far green ridges of the youthful Republic, ablaze with the unbroken tropical sunshine. The whirr of a telephone bell broke in upon his meditation.

arxiv-2107-03735.title: Lattice thermal conductivity of half-Heuslers with density functional theory and machine learning: Enhancing predictivity by active sampling with principal component analysis Journal: Computational Materials Science
arxiv-2107-03735.creator: Rasmus Tranås, Ole Martin Løvvik, Oliver Tomic, Kristian Berland
arxiv-2107-03735.description: Abstract Low lattice thermal conductivity is essential for high thermoelectric performance of a material. Lattice thermal conductivity is often computed using density functional theory (DFT), typically at a high computational cost. Training machine learning models to predict lattice thermal conductivity could offer an effective procedure to identify low lattice thermal conductivity compounds.

arxiv-2108-09684.title: Rainfall-runoff prediction using a Gustafson-Kessel clustering based Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy model
arxiv-2108-09684.creator: Subhrasankha Dey*, Tanmoy Dam
arxiv-2108-09684.description: Abstract A rainfall-runoff model predicts surface runoff either using a physically-based approach or using a systems-based approach. Takagi-Sugeno (TS) Fuzzy models are systems-based approaches and a popular modeling choice for hydrologists in recent decades due to several advantages and improved accuracy in prediction over other existing models.

arxiv-2111-09000.title: Toward a quantum computing algorithm to quantify classical and quantum correlation of system states
arxiv-2111-09000.creator: M. Mahdian, H. Davoodi Yeganeh
arxiv-2111-09000.description: Abstract Optimal measurement is required to obtain the quantum and classical correlations of a quantum state, and the crucial difficulty is how to acquire the maximal information about one system by measuring the other part; in other words, getting the maximum information corresponds to preparing the best measurement operators.

arxiv-2209-04308.title: Computational reproducibility of Jupyter notebooks from biomedical publications
arxiv-2209-04308.creator: Sheeba Samuel, Daniel Mietchen
arxiv-2209-04308.description: Abstract Jupyter notebooks allow to bundle executable code with its documentation and output in one interactive environment, and they represent a popular mechanism to document and share computational workflows, including for research publications. Here, we analyze the computational reproducibility of 9625 Jupyter notebooks from 1117 GitHub repositories associated with 1419 publications indexed in the biomedical literature repository PubMed Central.

arxiv-2212-12699.title: Quantum doubles of Fock type and bosonization Thanks: Pavel.Saponov@ihep.ru
arxiv-2212-12699.creator: Dimitry Gurevich
arxiv-2212-12699.description: Abstract We introduce analogs of creation and annihilation operators, related to involutive and Hecke symmetries R R , and perform bosonic and fermionic realization of the modified Reflection Equation algebras in terms of the so-called Quantum Doubles of Fock type.

arxiv-2309-04550.title: Retrieving Evidence from EHRs with LLMs: Possibilities and Challenges
arxiv-2309-04550.creator: Hiba Ahsan, Denis Jered McInerney, Jisoo Kim, Christopher Potter, Geoffrey Young, Silvio Amir, Byron C. Wallace
arxiv-2309-04550.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hiba Ahsan, Denis Jered McInerney, Jisoo Kim, Christopher Potter, Geoffrey Young, Silvio Amir, Byron C. Wallace. Unstructured data in Electronic Health Records (EHRs) often contains critical information—complementary to imaging—that could inform radiologists’ diagnoses. But the large volume of notes often associated with patients together with time constraints renders manually identifying relevant evidence practically infeasible.

arxiv-2401-00553.title: On Cohomology group of current Lie algebras
arxiv-2401-00553.creator: R. García-Delgado
arxiv-2401-00553.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by R. García-Delgado. In this work we state a result that relates the cohomology groups of a Lie algebra 𝔤 \mathfrak{g} and a current Lie algebra 𝔤 ⊗ 𝒮 \mathfrak{g}\otimes\mathcal{S} , by means of a short exact sequence – similar to the universal coefficients theorem for modules –, where 𝒮 \mathcal{S} is a finite dimensional, commutative and associative algebra with unit over a field 𝔽 \mathbb{F} .

arxiv-2507-19592.title: SurgPIS: Surgical-instrument-level Instances and Part-level Semantics for Weakly-supervised Part-aware Instance Segmentation
arxiv-2507-19592.creator: Meng Wei, Charlie Budd, Oluwatosin Alabi, Miaojing Shi, Tom Vercauteren
arxiv-2507-19592.description: Abstract Consistent surgical instrument segmentation is critical for automation in robot-assisted surgery. Yet, existing methods only treat instrument-level instance segmentation (IIS)or part-level semantic segmentation (PSS)separately, without interaction between these tasks. In this work, we formulate surgical tool segmentation as a unified part-aware instance segmentation (PIS)problem and introduce SurgPIS, the first PISmodel for surgical instruments.

arxiv-2509-00798.title: Multimodal Iterative RAG for Knowledge-Intensive Visual Question Answering
arxiv-2509-00798.creator: Changin Choi, Wonseok Lee, Jungmin Ko, Wonjong Rhee
arxiv-2509-00798.description: Abstract Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly enhanced the ability of these models in multimodal understanding and reasoning. However, the performance of MLLMs for knowledge-intensive visual questions, which require external knowledge beyond the visual content of an image, still remains limited.

arxiv-2509-13686.title: RF-LSCM: Pushing Radiance Fields to Multi-Domain Localized Statistical Channel Modeling for Cellular Network Optimization Thanks: Manuscript created June, 2025; Bingsheng Peng, Xinyu Qin are with the School of Science and Engineering, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen 518172, China, and
arxiv-2509-13686.creator: Bingsheng Peng, Shutao Zhang, Xi Zheng, Ye Xue, Xinyu Qin
arxiv-2509-13686.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Bingsheng Peng, Shutao Zhang, Xi Zheng, Ye Xue, Xinyu Qin. Accurate localized wireless channel modeling is a cornerstone of cellular network optimization, enabling reliable prediction of network performance during parameter tuning. Localized statistical channel modeling (LSCM) is the state-of-the-art channel modeling framework tailored for cellular network optimization.

arxiv-2509-22202.title: Library Hallucinations in LLMs: Risk Analysis Grounded in Developer Queries
arxiv-2509-22202.creator: Lukas Twist, Jie M. Zhang, Mark Harman, Helen Yannakoudakis
arxiv-2509-22202.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate code, yet they continue to hallucinate, often inventing non-existent libraries. Such library hallucinations are not just benign errors: they can mislead developers, break builds, and expose systems to supply chain threats such as slopsquatting.

britannica-1911-starch.title: Starch (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-starch.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-starch.description: Article 'Starch' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. forming one of the most important and characteristic elements of plant life. It originates within the living vegetable cell through the formative activity of chlorophyll under the influence of light, and is consequently an unfailing characteristic of all plants containing that body.

pmc-10671392.title: Incidence and Risk Factors for Wound Revision after Surgical Treatment of Spinal Metastasis: A National Population-Based Study in South Korea
pmc-10671392.creator: Han-Dong Lee, Hae-Dong Jang, Jin-Sung Park, Nam-Su Chung, Hee-Woong Chung, Jin-Young Jun, Kyungdo Han, Jae-Young Hong
pmc-10671392.description: Wound complications are commonly seen after surgeries for metastatic spine tumors. While numerous studies have pinpointed various risk factors, there is ongoing debate. Therefore, this study aimed to verify various factors that are still under debate utilizing the comprehensive Korean National Health Insurance Service database.

pmc-11492918.title: Pattern and Prevalence of Retinal Vein Occlusion in Bhutan: A 3-Year National Survey at Vitreoretinal Clinics
pmc-11492918.creator: Bhim B Rai, Phuntsho Dorji, Ted Maddess
pmc-11492918.description: PurposeWe conducted this study to determine the pattern and prevalence of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) in Bhutan to inform national health policy as no data has been compiled previously.MethodsA retrospective cross-sectional survey was conducted over 3 years, including all new RVO cases. For patients with bilateral RVO, one eye was chosen randomly.

pmc-12418681.title: Early repolarization pattern with oral liquid nicotine
pmc-12418681.creator: Julian Wolfes, Lea Reitnauer, Lars Eckardt
pmc-12418681.description: While most sudden cardiac deaths are due to structural heart disease or cardiac ischemia, intoxications are rather rare and often unrecognized. Here we present a case of a 35-year-old patient who trickled cumulative 60 mg of the pure nicotine liquid. This led to cardiac arrest and ventricular fibrillation.

pmc-12781224.title: Evaluation of the Characteristics Associated With Methamphetamine Use in Patients With Heroin Use Disorder
pmc-12781224.creator: Zeki Vatansever, İzgi Alnıak, Tonguc D Berkol
pmc-12781224.description: Objective:This study compared addiction severity, psychotic symptoms, suicide risk, and craving in patients with heroin use disorder, with and without methamphetamine use. We also investigated the reasons for methamphetamine use in these patients, and assessed 3-month clinical follow-up and treatment compliance. Methods:This cross-sectional study included 166 inpatients diagnosed with heroin use disorder (DSM-5).

pmc-13166750.title: One-piece extended depth of focus intraocular lens implantation in the capsular bag in the presence of a posterior capsule rupture
pmc-13166750.creator: Adam Hatoum, Disha Singhania, Kirupakaran Arun, Victoria Cosgrove, Nizar Din, Mukhtar Bizrah
pmc-13166750.description: Introduction and importance:Posterior capsule rupture has historically prevented implantation of one-piece intraocular lenses in the bag. We present a case of extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens insertion into the capsular bag after posterior capsule rupture with an excellent post-operative outcome.Case presentation:The patient was a 64-year-old female presenting for bilateral refractive exchange to reduce dependence on spectacles.

pmc-13383902.title: Surgical Technique for Treating Focal Osteochondral Knee Lesions Using an Aragonite‐Based Biphasic Scaffold
pmc-13383902.creator: Eric Wang, Alexandra M. Cancio‐Bello, Katelyn T. Koschmeder, Bryn Berens, Anikar Chhabra
pmc-13383902.description: Osteochondral lesions of the knee, particularly in patients with early osteoarthritic changes, remain a clinical challenge. The Agili‐C implant (CartiHeal, Smith & Nephew), an aragonite‐based osteochondral scaffold, offers a single‐stage, off‐the‐shelf solution designed to regenerate both cartilage and subchondral bone.

pmc-13586419.title: Xenotransplantation of the Porcine Lung—From Immunological Barriers to Emerging Experimental Strategies
pmc-13586419.creator: Nathalie Roters, Niveditha Varma, Robert Ramm, Heiner Niemann, Patrick Zardo, Arjang Ruhparwar, Tobias Goecke
pmc-13586419.description: Lung transplantation is the only long‐lasting life‐saving treatment for patients with end‐stage pulmonary disease, but the ever‐growing shortage of suitable donor organs leads to high mortality rates of the afflicted patients. Xenotransplantation, the transplantation of organs across species, has emerged as a promising alternative.

pmc-13619951.title: Low nutrition literacy among 4th−5th graders in Chongqing, China: a wake-up call for school health and factors associated with nutrition literacy
pmc-13619951.creator: Yuanyuan Lan, Jiaxin Deng, Ailin Zhou, Yaocheng Luo, Huiyi Zhang, Wenhua Ran, Ling Liu, Zumin Shi, Yong Zhao
pmc-13619951.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveDespite growing global recognition that nutrition literacy in childhood is a cornerstone of healthy eating and long-term wellbeing, evidence from Chinese primary school settings—particularly from inland, rapidly urbanizing regions—remains scarce. This study aimed to assess the nutrition literacy level of 4th−5th graders in chongqing, china, and to identify its key influencing factors, thereby sounding a wake-up call for school-based health promotion that holds relevance beyond the local context.MethodsA multistage stratified cluster sampling method was used to conduct a cross-sectional online survey of

pmc-13632109.title: Calcium signaling in human and mouse microglia exhibit differential susceptibility to phytocannabinoids
pmc-13632109.creator: Ivana Pilchova, Andrea Fleig, Reinhold Penner
pmc-13632109.description: BackgroundNeurological disorders affect over 40% of the global population and are driven in part by microglia-mediated neuroinflammation that depends on calcium (Ca²⁺) signaling. Cannabis-derived compounds (CBx) modulate microglial activation and cytokine release, however, the impact of understudied CBx on Ca2+ signaling pathways controlling inflammatory responses remains largely unknown.

pmc-13637263.title: Functional decline in the final years of life: A multicohort study
pmc-13637263.creator: Junjie Lin, Mika Kivimäki, Yue Zhang, Yaguan Zhou, Xiaolin Xu
pmc-13637263.description: BackgroundPhysical, cognitive, and psychological conditions are associated with an increased risk of mortality, yet few studies have characterized terminal declines in these functional domains preceding death. In this multicohort study, we examined both separate and joint trajectories of physical, cognitive, and psychological functioning during the final decade of life and assessed the role of socioeconomic status (SES).

pmc-13647596.title: SORDINO: silent, sensitive, specific and artifact-resistant fMRI in awake, behaving mice
pmc-13647596.creator: Martin J. MacKinnon, Sheng Song, Tzu-Hao Harry Chao, Li-Ming Hsu, Scott T. Albert, Yuncong Ma, Tatiana A. Shnitko, Tzu-Wen Winnie Wang, Randy J. Nonneman, Corey D. Freeman, Samuel Booth, Siddhi S. Ozarkar, Paul B. Manis, Uzay E. Emir, Eric R. Muir, Mark D. Shen, Benjamin D. Philpot, Adam W. Hantman,
pmc-13647596.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Blood-oxygenation-level-dependent (BOLD) functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has advanced brain mapping across species. This widely used technique, however, faces challenges such as acoustic noise, electromagnetic interference, motion artifacts, magnetic-field inhomogeneity and limitations in sensitivity and specificity. Here we introduce Steady-state On-the-Ramp Detection of INduction-decay with Oversampling (SORDINO), an improved zero echo time (ZTE)-based fMRI technique that maintains ultra-low slew rate and acquires data exclusively during gradient direction changes.
